name: Design and build landfill site
fact: Landfill design must address stability, lining, capping and environmental risk assessments as part of permitting.
gate: Design intent or submitted assessment is not constructed performance or permit compliance.

name: Landfills for inert waste
fact: Inert landfill closure/aftercare requires stability monitoring and written Environment Agency agreement before monitoring can cease where required.
gate: Inert-waste status does not mean zero ground-gas, settlement or stability risk.

name: Close your landfill site
fact: A landfill is definitely closed only after Environment Agency written agreement; closure, aftercare and permit surrender are separate stages.
gate: Stopping waste acceptance or being 'closed' does not equal surrendered permit or development-ready land.

name: Landfill aftercare and permit surrender
fact: Guidance updated 17 June 2026 requires evidence of acceptable pollution risk, stability and aftercare before permit surrender; active controls can prevent surrender.
gate: Beneficial use or planning permission on a closed landfill does not itself prove the environmental permit can be surrendered.

name: Landfill sector technical guidance
fact: Environment Agency landfill technical collection links gas, leachate, groundwater, surface-water and surrender guidance.
gate: Monitoring guidance or one monitoring result is not a complete site-stability/pollution conclusion.

name: Planning applications and Coal Mining Risk Assessments
fact: Most development in a coalfield Development High Risk Area requires a Coal Mining Risk Assessment; mine-entry locations may need intrusive investigation and no-build zones.
gate: High-risk-area mapping is a screening trigger, not a confirmed mine-entry location or proof a layout is safe.

name: Coalfield planning advice service
fact: Mining Remediation Authority planning-advice service was updated 25 June 2026 for proposals in the Development High Risk Area.
gate: Pre-application advice is not planning approval, permission to disturb coal features or remediation verification.

name: Detailed coalfield planning advice
fact: Detailed June 2026 advice helps identify mining legacy risk but states the developer remains responsible for ensuring development is safe and stable.
gate: Authority advice cannot be treated as a warranty of ground conditions.

name: Building over or near a mine entry policy
fact: Mining Remediation Authority policy says building over or within the influencing distance of a mine entry should be avoided where possible and requires specialist design/permissions where proposed.
gate: Mine-entry treatment records or capping do not automatically make close-proximity building acceptable.

name: Home extensions in former coal mining areas
fact: Current guidance warns about mine entries, mine gas and ground stability and recommends specialist assessment where source-pathway-receptor risks may exist.
gate: A domestic-scale project or absence of known records does not eliminate unrecorded mining hazards.

name: Free coal mining information
fact: Mining Remediation Authority map viewer and WMS expose selected coal-mining information from the national database.
gate: Free map-viewer data is screening information and not a substitute for detailed searches or intrusive investigation.

name: Access coal mining information and data
fact: Guidance published 16 July 2026 describes current access to mine plans, licence registers, deeds, geological data and detailed searches.
gate: Access to historical records does not establish the current physical condition of a parcel.

name: Coal mining records, data, deeds and documents
fact: Mining Remediation Authority holds historical digital and paper coal-mining records used for desktop research and development studies.
gate: Historical records may be incomplete and do not replace site-specific geotechnical/mining investigation.

name: Mining Remediation Authority licences and agreements 2026
fact: The 2026 licences and agreements page was updated 24 June 2026 and records authority-issued mining permissions/agreements.
gate: Licence or incidental-coal agreement status is not planning permission or evidence remediation is complete.

name: BGS GeoSure
fact: BGS GeoSure provides 1:50,000 susceptibility data for six natural ground-stability hazards used to support planning and property assessment.
gate: GeoSure identifies potential hazard, not site-specific probability of failure, engineering design or foundation adequacy.

name: BGS GeoSure 5 km hex grid
fact: Open GeoSure 5 km hex data generalises six hazards into low, moderate and significant classes over roughly 65 km² cells.
gate: A 5 km class is regional screening only and must not be transferred to an exact parcel or foundation design.

name: BGS GeoSure shrink-swell
fact: BGS maps shrink-swell potential at 1:50,000 using geological and engineering information.
gate: Susceptibility does not replace boreholes, soil testing, tree/water assessment or foundation design.

name: BGS GeoSure soluble rocks
fact: BGS maps potential dissolution-related ground instability in soluble rocks such as chalk, gypsum and salt.
gate: Map class is not proof of a cavity or sinkhole beneath a development footprint.

name: BGS GeoSure collapsible deposits
fact: BGS assesses collapsible-ground potential at 1:50,000 using superficial geology and engineering evidence.
gate: Potential collapse requires site-specific ground investigation before engineering conclusions.

name: BGS GeoSure compressible ground
fact: BGS maps potential compressible ground such as peat, alluvium and soft clays at 1:50,000.
gate: Mapped potential does not quantify settlement under the proposed building loads.

name: BGS GeoSure landslides
fact: BGS GeoSure landslides uses geology, slope, geotechnical data and landslide records to map susceptibility and explicitly does not determine temporal landslide risk.
gate: Susceptibility class must not be treated as an active landslide or a predicted failure date.

name: BGS GeoSure running sand
fact: BGS maps running-sand potential where water can fluidise loosely packed sandy layers, particularly around excavation or groundwater changes.
gate: Map potential is not proof running sand will occur under the proposed excavation.

name: BGS National Landslide Database
fact: The BGS National Landslide Database contains over 17,000 reported landslide records and each point is a reference to a reported event.
gate: No nearby database point does not prove no landslide susceptibility, and a point is not an exact active boundary.

name: UKradon home
fact: UKHSA's UKradon service separates area checking, building measurement and mitigation into check-measure-act steps.
gate: Being in an Affected Area is not a measured indoor radon concentration for a specific building.

name: UKradon radon searches
fact: UKradon distinguishes indicative 1 km/postcode information from definitive address searches and recommends testing in Affected Areas.
gate: Indicative map band or address probability is not a measured annual radon level or proof mitigation is required/sufficient.
